' (GNNs) ability to accurately learn node representations heavily relies on their ability to propagate information effectively. This study delves into the theoretical underpinnings of the information propagation process in GNNs, specifically examining the limits of their ability to transmit information between distant nodes. We demonstrate that standard GNNs have a fundamental information transmission limitation, which is directly proportional to the number of nodes and the number of node features. This finding is further substantiated by the presentation of a specific graph and set of node features that allows for the accurate transmission of a substantial amount of information between any two nodes. We also introduce an advanced GNN architecture, referred to as the hyperbolic GNN, which is capable of overcoming the aforementioned information transmission limitation. This new architecture leverages the properties of hyperbolic spaces to facilitate more efficient information propagation and is theoretically proven to be superior to standard GNNs. Experimental results show that hyperbolic GNNs outperform standard GNNs on real-world datasets. The study's code and accompanying datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/alexandrosk/hyperbolic_gnn.
